what: Golden values from the independent Python reference. The JavaScript engine is tested against these; they were NOT produced by it. Regenerate with `build`, verify with `--check`.

perft.name: start
kiwipete
queen is the only royal; two bishops tie on distance (b2, f2), lower file wins on a rook capture on d4
two bishops tie on distance AND file (d2, d6), lower rank wins; a rook on h4 takes the queen on d4
squared straight-line distance, not king-steps: g7 is 3 steps away, h4 is 4, yet h4 is closer (16 against 18)
squared straight-line distance, not city-block: f6 is 4 blocks away, a4 is 3, yet f6 is closer (8 against 9)
class order beats distance: a far bishop is crowned although a knight stands next to the queen
a queen captured while the king lives: nothing is crowned
no bishop: the closest knight is crowned
no bishop or knight: the closest rook is crowned
only pawns left behind: the closest pawn is crowned
king captured while a queen lives: nothing changes
pawn about to promote with no king piece: a king is among the choices
pawn about to promote WITH a king piece: no king choice
en passant with royals en prise
boxed in: the king on a8 cannot move and nor can pawns a7, b7, b8, so it sacrifices itself and the closest pawn (a7 and b8 tie, the lower file wins) is crowned
boxed in with a queen as the only royal: the queen sacrifices itself and a pawn is crowned
never offered when an ordinary move exists: the king is boxed in but the queen can move
several queens and no king left: nothing changes and every queen stays a queen
a boxed-in king beside a boxed-in queen: the king sacrifices itself, the queen takes command, no pawn is crowned
two boxed-in queens and no king: the queen on the lowest file (a8) sacrifices itself, the other stays a queen
two boxed-in queens on the same file and no king: the lower rank (a7) sacrifices itself, the queen on a8 stays

showdown.name: a showdown that has just begun: only the two starting squares are touched
a slide may pass over a touched square (b2) but not land on it; the corner king still reaches c3
a capture is exempt: the enemy queen stands on a touched square and the king may still take it
every one of the 27 squares the king on d4 could reach is touched: it has no ordinary move, so it sacrifices itself and loses
a late showdown: three untouched squares (f6, b2, a1) are all the king has left

repeat.name: the second occurrence is allowed, the third is refused: Kb1-b2 would be the third time, Kb1-a1 only the second
every ordinary move would be a third occurrence and there is no pawn move or capture to fall back on, so the royal sacrifices
a pawn move and a capture are never refused however often the position has been seen; the king's quiet moves are
nothing seen yet: the list is exactly the ordinary legal moves
